blueprint_refs: SBI calibration uses ONLY the single observed trajectory from training set (trajectory_id=0)
evaluate the inferred parameters on full train/val/test sets

evidence.metrics: train_loss=222.89 while val_loss=344.54 and test_loss=305.38 (large generalization gap)

single-trajectory-sbi-limits-generalizat.error_identification: Validation and test MSE are substantially higher than training MSE, indicating the inferred (beta,gamma) from a single observed trajectory does not transfer well to the other trajectories.
single-trajectory-sbi-limits-generalizat.root_cause_analysis: The blueprint intentionally constrains calibration to one observed trajectory (trajectory_id=0). With only two global parameters (beta,gamma) and stochastic dynamics, a posterior fit to a single realization can be poorly representative of the broader dataset distribution, yielding a persistent val/test gap regardless of NPE conditioning improvements.
single-trajectory-sbi-limits-generalizat.correct_approach: Within the blueprint constraint (must condition on a single observed trajectory), reduce estimator variance and improve identifiability: (1) in SBINPECalibrator.fit, augment x with a small set of deterministic, low-dimensional summary features computed from the same flattened trajectory (e.g., peak I, time of peak, final size R_T, early growth rate proxy), concatenated to the flattened vector before z-scoring; (2) use multiple independent simulator RNG streams per theta for the k_cal_rollouts loop (see separate issue) so the mean trajectory is an unbiased mean rather than a correlated sample path; (3) optionally increase num_simulations adaptively when posterior samples have high variance (log posterior std) to avoid under-training. Realistically, achieving val_loss <= 1e-6 is not plausible given stochasticity, model mismatch across trajectories, and only two parameters inferred from one trajectory.
single-trajectory-sbi-limits-generalizat.key_insight: If calibration is constrained to one stochastic trajectory, add stable summary features and variance-reduction to the simulator-to-x mapping; otherwise posterior mean will not generalize even when training loss looks acceptable.

blueprint_refs: For each θ, ... roll out T steps ... Collect (θ, x) pairs.
optionally run K stochastic rollouts per trajectory and output the mean predicted trajectory

evidence.metrics: val_loss remains high (344.54) despite using k_cal_rollouts_per_theta=5, suggesting limited variance reduction

correlated-rollouts-per-theta-reuse-same.error_identification: The code averages 5 rollouts per theta during SBI data generation, but those rollouts are not statistically independent because they share a single simulator RNG that continues sequentially across rollouts and across thetas.
correlated-rollouts-per-theta-reuse-same.root_cause_analysis: In SBINPECalibrator.fit, a single DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator(self._rng) instance is created once, and simulator.step draws from the same underlying numpy Generator for every step. The inner loop over k_cal_rollouts does not reset or split RNG state per rollout, producing correlated rollouts and reducing the intended variance-reduction effect of averaging.
correlated-rollouts-per-theta-reuse-same.correct_approach: In SBINPECalibrator.fit, create independent RNG streams per rollout and (ideally) per theta: derive a fresh numpy Generator for each rollout using spawned SeedSequence from the base seed (or use self._rng.integers to seed a new Generator) and instantiate a new DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator with that generator inside the rollout loop. Keep evaluation rollouts similarly independent (see next issue) for consistent mean-of-K behavior.
correlated-rollouts-per-theta-reuse-same.key_insight: Averaging K rollouts only reduces noise if rollouts are independent; never reuse one RNG stream across rollouts when the intent is Monte Carlo mean estimation.

blueprint_refs: for each trajectory ... simulate K rollouts ... compute mean predicted trajectory
evaluation-rollouts-not-independent-acro.error_identification: Mean predictions are computed from multiple rollouts, but all rollouts for all trajectories share the same simulator RNG stream, which can induce subtle correlations and reduce effective sample size for Monte Carlo means.
evaluation-rollouts-not-independent-acro.root_cause_analysis: In main, DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator is instantiated once with rng=rng. In DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator.rollout, repeated calls to step for different (trajectory_id, rollout k) all pull from the same generator without splitting or re-seeding, so randomness is shared sequentially across the entire evaluation set.
evaluation-rollouts-not-independent-acro.correct_approach: Modify DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator.rollout to either: (1) accept a base_seed and spawn per-(trajectory_id, k) generators; or (2) instantiate a separate DiscreteTimeSIRSimulator with its own Generator per trajectory and per rollout. This improves stability of the predicted mean trajectory and reduces evaluation noise, especially for small K or when comparing many trajectories.
evaluation-rollouts-not-independent-acro.key_insight: For mean-of-K evaluation, independence across rollouts (and ideally across trajectories) matters; otherwise K does not translate to K effective samples.

blueprint_refs: This setup intentionally does NOT split time into train/val within a trajectory.
SBI calibration uses ONLY train trajectory_id==0 as the single observation x_o.

evidence.metrics: No direct metric symptom; structural/spec mismatch risk

holdout-split-implemented-but-unused-and.error_identification: A train_fraction-based holdout split is created even though the blueprint explicitly says no within-trajectory temporal holdout is required; the calibrator ignores it, but the presence of dead/contradicting logic increases maintenance risk and confusion during further iterations.
holdout-split-implemented-but-unused-and.root_cause_analysis: holdout_split creates prefix/suffix segments for each train trajectory, but SBINPECalibrator.fit explicitly discards holdout ("_ = holdout") and always uses the full trajectory_id==0. This is inconsistent with blueprint intent and makes it easier to accidentally introduce leakage/incorrect evaluation later.
holdout-split-implemented-but-unused-and.correct_approach: Remove the holdout_split call and the HoldoutBundle plumbing entirely, or refactor BaseCalibrator.fit signature to not require holdout. If you must keep the type for compatibility, at least rename and document it as unused, and add an assertion in main that no temporal split is applied to observation trajectory_id==0.
holdout-split-implemented-but-unused-and.key_insight: Eliminate dead code paths that contradict the spec; they don’t help metrics and they increase the chance of accidental evaluation protocol drift.

evidence.metrics: Program emits keys train_loss/val_loss/test_loss rather than train_mse_overall/val_mse_overall/test_mse_overall in results.json

missing-blueprint-metrics-schema-in-resu.error_identification: The output JSON metric keys do not match the blueprint’s io_contract.metrics_schema naming (mse_overall naming), which can break downstream evaluators even if internal metrics are correct.
missing-blueprint-metrics-schema-in-resu.root_cause_analysis: Evaluator.compute_metrics returns keys named train_loss/val_loss/test_loss and save_results writes them verbatim. The blueprint’s io_contract expects train_mse_overall/val_mse_overall/test_mse_overall (and conservation_violation_rate without the 'val_' prefix).
missing-blueprint-metrics-schema-in-resu.correct_approach: In Evaluator.compute_metrics and/or save_results, map internal metric names to the blueprint’s required schema keys (while optionally keeping aliases). Ensure conservation metric key matches the io_contract exactly. This is an interface fix; it won’t change MSE values but will improve compliance.
missing-blueprint-metrics-schema-in-resu.key_insight: Match output schemas exactly; metric naming mismatches are silent integration failures that won’t show up as runtime errors.
